doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Writing dystopic songs at eighty
summary: The bass clarinet doubling, then his recent dystopic songs, Mose Allison's cynicism and nostalgia.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah and the bass clarinet doubling the bass parts, very cool.
Later today if you went out to continue your day, what kind of things might you hear or see that could lead to a song title and a song?

Well today, let’s see — I’m trying to think the last few songs I wrote here where I am. That’s funny — not funny — but this last year I turned 80 and I started writing some very dystopic songs. I mean I’ve always — you know people accused Mose Allison of being cynical. And he would say, “I’m not cynical I’m just telling it like it is.” And I would always have to kind of half apologize after singing one of my songs like “I may be wrong but it sure seems to me the past ain’t what it was and the future ain’t what it used to be.” So I just fell down this dystopic hole and why did I do that? You know I don’t even watch the news anymore and I think that’s part of it you know. The world has become such a deranged, inhuman place that everywhere you turn you have to confront humanity in a much larger frame than you would back in the day before there was such an onslaught of media where you could still talk about a boy and a girl holding hands and going on a date and that would be relevant. But now you can’t — how could you write a song like that? You know if I go out my door at some point I’m going to see some homeless people. If I go out my door I’m going to hear some really cheesy popular music that is everywhere. I mean it makes me think a lot about the past. I makes me feel older. And so I guess I’m saying if I go out and have an experience I come back there’d probably be something nostalgic in the song I wrote that would probably be something, I don’t know, I’m getting closer to Leonard Cohen every day.
